attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL 9) using Team RabbitMQ's official Cloudsmith repos for Erlang 26 and rabbitmq-server. Created a dedicated CA on node1 (4096-bit RSA, 10y validity) that issued per-node server certs (SANs for hostname+IP) and one client cert. AMQP is served exclusively over TLS on 5671 (plaintext 5672 disabled via listeners.tcp=none) with verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, so only clients presenting a certificate signed by the cluster CA can connect — verified positively (successful publish/consume with the CA-issued client cert) and negatively (TLS alert 'certificate_required' with no cert, 'unknown_ca' alert with a cert from a different CA). The management HTTP API (15672) is bound only to each node's private cluster IP (not 0.0.0.0) and additionally firewalld-restricted (rich rules) to the 10.100.130.0/24 cluster subnet, with the public zone otherwise deny-by-default — confirmed reachable from a cluster peer (node2→node1 returned HTTP 401, i.e. TCP+HTTP reached the API) while not exposed on any other interface. Cluster formed via rabbitmqctl join_cluster with a shared Erlang cookie; cluster_status confirms all 3 nodes running with no partitions. Completed the mandatory rolling-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and RabbitMQ/cluster health per node, restarted node2 → node3 → node1 one at a time (each `reboot` acknowledged before disconnect), polled until each came back, and proved a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id per node. After each restart verified RabbitMQ auto-started, cluster membership and a durable quorum queue (created with a test message before the restarts) remained healthy/online with the message intact throughout, and confirmed TLS+client-cert enforcement and firewall/management restrictions were unaffected after the full cycle. All credentials (Erlang cookie, testadmin password) were generated on-node and never appeared as literals in tool commands (passed via command substitution reading root-only files).
